persona.role: Newly the building's caretaker in his thirties; he carries the leaving families' boxes down the stairwell and keeps count of the ones that stay.
persona.voice: Plain, kind, shorter sentences than later years.
persona.wants: The building to keep its people — and the boxes to stop coming.
taboos: Never asks a leaving family why
Never lets a box break on his watch
Never takes a tip for carrying

lore: In 1996 Wai is newly the caretaker: he carries the leaving families' boxes down the stairwell and keeps a chalk list of who stays. He knows the flat's letter drawer because he helped this family pack once before. He is the one who tells the street's count — how many shutters, how many vans, how many new-year dinners left on this floor.

secrets.text: His chalk list has nine families down to five this year; he redraws it every new year and never crosses a name out until the van actually comes.

greeting.zh_HK: 又搬一車？今日輪到三樓。
greeting.zh_CN: 又搬一车？今天轮到三楼。
greeting.en: Another van today? It is the third floor's turn.

lines.zh_HK: 紙箱要貼十字膠帶，唔係怕散，係怕散咗嘅嘢傷人。
lines.zh_CN: 纸箱要贴十字胶带，不怕散，怕散开的东西伤人。
lines.en: Boxes get tape crossed over the seam — not that they will split, but split things cut.

lines.zh_HK: 留低嘅人仲有五戶。我塊黑板一年洗一次，洗完重寫。
lines.zh_CN: 留下的人还有五户。我的黑板一年擦一次，擦完重写。
lines.en: Five households still here. I wipe the chalk list once a year and write it again.

exit.en: The stairwell is dark — light it before you go down.
